provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Number names 1 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state number names 1 to 10.
The pupils should be able to match number words to numerals.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers 1 to 10.
Today we will learn their names.

Content:
One is 1. Two is 2. Three is 3.
Four is 4. Five is 5. Six is 6.
Seven is 7. Eight is 8. Nine is 9.
Ten is 10. Let us say them together.

Class activity:
Give each pupil number cards.
Teacher calls a number. Pupils hold up the correct card.

Evaluation questions:
What number name comes after five?
Show me the card for seven.
Count to ten.

Summary:
We can now say number names from one to ten.

topics.title: Number names 11 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state number names 11 to 20.
The pupils should be able to match number words to numerals.

Introduction:
We know numbers 1 to 10.
Today we learn numbers 11 to 20.

Content:
Eleven is 11. Twelve is 12. Thirteen is 13.
Fourteen is 14. Fifteen is 15. Sixteen is 16.
Seventeen is 17. Eighteen is 18. Nineteen is 19.
Twenty is 20. Let us clap and count.

Class activity:
Pupils line up. Each says a number name from 11 to 20.

Evaluation questions:
What number name comes after fifteen?
Show me the card for eighteen.
Count from eleven to twenty.

Summary:
We can now say number names from eleven to twenty.

topics.title: Ordinal numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify ordinal numbers first to tenth.
The pupils should be able to state their position in a line.

Introduction:
We know numbers for counting.
Today we learn numbers for position.

Content:
First is 1st. Second is 2nd. Third is 3rd.
Fourth is 4th. Fifth is 5th. Sixth is 6th.
Seventh is 7th. Eighth is 8th. Ninth is 9th.
Tenth is 10th. We use these for order.

Class activity:
Pupils line up. Teacher asks who is first, second, third.

Evaluation questions:
What comes after third?
Stand in the fifth position.
Who is last in our line?

Summary:
We can now use ordinal numbers for position.

topics.title: Adding to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to solve addition problems to 10.
The pupils should be able to write addition sentences.

Introduction:
We can count numbers.
Today we add numbers to make ten.

Content:
Addition means putting together. 1 + 9 = 10.
2 + 8 = 10. 3 + 7 = 10. 4 + 6 = 10.
5 + 5 = 10. 6 + 4 = 10. 7 + 3 = 10.
8 + 2 = 10. 9 + 1 = 10. 10 + 0 = 10.

Class activity:
Pupils use fingers to show addition facts to ten.

Evaluation questions:
What is 3 + 7?
Show me 5 + 5 with your fingers.
Write the addition for 4 + 6.

Summary:
We can now add numbers to make ten.

topics.title: Adding to 20 without carrying
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to solve addition to 20 without carrying.
The pupils should be able to write addition sentences.

Introduction:
We know how to add to ten.
Today we add bigger numbers.

Content:
12 + 5 = 17. We count on from 12.
13 + 4 = 17. 14 + 3 = 17. 15 + 2 = 17.
16 + 1 = 17. Use counters to see.

Class activity:
Pupils use bottle caps to solve addition problems.

Evaluation questions:
What is 12 + 5?
Show me 13 + 4 with counters.
Solve 15 + 2.

Summary:
We can now add numbers to 20 without carrying.

topics.title: Subtraction from 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to solve subtraction from 10.
The pupils should be able to write subtraction sentences.

Introduction:
We know how to add.
Today we take away.

Content:
Subtraction means taking away. 10-1 = 9.
10-2 = 8. 10-3 = 7. 10-4 = 6.
10-5 = 5. 10-6 = 4. 10-7 = 3.
10-8 = 2. 10-9 = 1. 10-10 = 0.

Class activity:
Pupils use sweets to show subtraction stories.

Evaluation questions:
What is 10-3?
Show me 10-5 with sweets.
Write the subtraction for 10-7.

Summary:
We can now subtract from ten.

topics.title: Doubling
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to double numbers to 10.
The pupils should be able to solve doubling problems.

Introduction:
We know how to add numbers.
Today we learn to double.

Content:
Double means add the same number. Double 1 is 2.
Double 2 is 4. Double 3 is 6. Double 4 is 8.
Double 5 is 10. Double 6 is 12. Double 7 is 14.
Double 8 is 16. Double 9 is 18. Double 10 is 20.

Class activity:
Pupils play the double dots game with a dice.

Evaluation questions:
What is double 3?
Show me double 4 with dots.
Solve double 5.

Summary:
We can now double numbers to ten.

topics.title: Sharing equally
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to share items equally.
The pupils should be able to find half of a number.

Introduction:
We know how to double.
Today we learn to share.

Content:
Sharing equally means giving the same to each.
Share 10 sweets between 2 friends. Each gets 5.
Half of 10 is 5. Half of 8 is 4. Half of 6 is 3.
Half of 4 is 2. Half of 2 is 1.

Class activity:
Pupils share pencils between two friends equally.

Evaluation questions:
Share 8 sweets between 2 friends.
What is half of 6?
Show me half of 4 with counters.

Summary:
We can now share equally and find half.

topics.title: Money play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count naira up to 20.
The pupils should be able to buy items and get change.

Introduction:
We know numbers and adding.
Today we use money to buy things.

Content:
Naira is our money. We have 1 naira, 2 naira, 5 naira, 10 naira.
If something costs 15 naira and you pay 20 naira.
You get 5 naira back. That is change.

Class activity:
Pupils play shop with naira notes and buy items.

Evaluation questions:
What coin makes 10 naira?
Buy a pen for 12 naira with 20 naira.
How much change will you get?

Summary:
We can now use naira to buy things.

topics.title: Revision and maths olympics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to solve mixed addition and subtraction.
The pupils should be able to play number games.

Introduction:
We have learned many things in maths.
Today we play games to show what we know.

Content:\ Mixed addition and subtraction to 20.
Counting to 20. Number names to 20.
Doubling and sharing. Using naira.

Class activity:
Pupils play maths olympics games with points.

Evaluation questions:
What is 10 + 5?
Show me half of 8.
Buy a book for 18 naira with 20 naira.

Summary:
We are all maths stars now.
